content.thinking:
I'm checking whether anyone noticed the problem: shoppers' stored monthly totals no longer match their purchases, and the monthly statement would display those wrong totals. The record doesn't mention any complaints, so the issue seems to have surfaced through the spend-integrity check rather than from users.

I'm settling on a wording for the symptom: nothing visibly failed for shoppers, but their stored monthly spend totals stopped matching their purchases. I'm keeping it under sixteen words and leaving out any figures, then moving on to the causal chain.

I'm tracing the cause back to the deploy: since the onset, purchases have still been appended, but the stored month total no longer moves with them. The later deploy removed that update from the purchase path, and I'm checking that P1 is ruled out because the alert dates the earliest affected purchase after P2.

I'm ruling out a flag flip too: the flags read in the hour before the alert show no changes, so nothing toggled. The last step of the chain is that the change stopped writing the month total but left the stored field in place, while the statement and summary code still treat that field as the month's spend.

I'm checking the root cause against the code: the P2 revision dropped the month-total update from record_purchase, while the statement, summary, and reconciliation code still read the stored field. Each purchase since then leaves that total short by its price, and the readers and diff bear that out. On the deriving path, both versions drop the update, so the flag value doesn't matter there.

I'm checking whether the rollback covers the deriving path too. The rollback restores record_purchase, but the diff only touches that function, so record_purchase_deriving_the_month probably skips the month update before and after, and it would stay broken behind the derive_the_month flag.

I'm checking whether the rollback fully covers the deriving path. The diff only changes record_purchase, so record_purchase_deriving_the_month likely skips the month update both before and after, leaving purchases that go through that path still drifting behind the derive_the_month flag. I also need to note that the stored month totals already written short stay wrong, since the repair script hasn't been run.

I'm listing the contributing factors now: the spend-integrity check only runs weekly, so the drift sat undetected for most of the period, and no alert paged anyone, which a person could have acted on sooner.

I'm checking whether the test suite would have caught this: the test file on main pins that record_purchase adds to the month total, but that file was run at 26f1d7e, where record_purchase no longer moves the month, so the test didn't catch the regression.

I'm listing another contributing factor: a test that pins the month total update already sits in the test file at the deployed revision, yet no run of the tests before the deploy shows up, so the deploy pipeline should require the suite to pass first.

I'm weighing whether the missing review of the change to the purchase ledger belongs in the list as its own factor, since that module's docstring warns that a write moving one total and not the other leaves two answers. I'm also noting that nothing on the write path checks for drift, so a write-time invariant could have caught the first bad purchase, though that overlaps with the check-cadence factor and may fold into it.

I'm weighing whether a missing paging route counts as its own contributing factor, since the alert fired but no person was notified to act on it. I'm also setting aside the latent deriving-path fault: it isn't part of this incident, and the fix already on main covers it.

I'm weighing whether a missing paging route counts as its own factor, since the alert fired but no person was notified to act on it, and I'm setting aside the latent deriving-path fault because it isn't part of this incident.

I'm listing what the team got right: Argus took up the incident and called in the Investigator, which tied the onset to the P2 deploy and checked that every replica was on that revision. I'm also noting that Argus checked the flag history and declined to roll back an action it couldn't verify, while still recommending it. The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request, along with a one-off repair script that reports by default.

I'm working out the remaining action items: the repair script needs a report-mode run against a same-month export so I can check its list against the accounts the alert flagged, and the corrected totals still have to be applied and loaded back.

I'm turning to the follow-up actions: correcting the stored month totals for the affected accounts, running the repair script on an export from this month and loading the results back. I'm also noting that the spend-integrity check should run far more often than its current cadence so drift is caught sooner, and that on-call should be paged when the reconciliation alert fires.

I'm noting that the fixes need to be deployed, and the rollback and the fix each depend on that deploy going out. I'm also weighing the assumptions: I can't confirm that the affected accounts all fall in the current month, and I don't have evidence either way on whether any shopper saw a wrong monthly statement.

I'm weighing the cause description now: the code change stopped updating each shopper's saved monthly total at purchase time, while the display and checks still read that saved figure, which I've confirmed rather than guessed.

I'm laying out the mechanism now: the spend-integrity check caught stored month totals disagreeing with the purchases behind them, with no visible failure for shoppers. The write path from deploy P2 stopped moving the account's month total, so whichever path a purchase took, the month figure stayed put while the lifetime total kept growing. I'm also noting that all replicas were on that revision once they rolled out.

I'm working out the mechanism behind the drift: a code change stopped writing each account's month total, but the statement, summary and reconciliation code still read that stored figure as the month's spend.

action_items.item: Correct the stored month totals of the affected accounts once a fixed or rolled-back revision is running, for example with the repair script Code-Fix proposed: run it with --apply on an account export taken in the same month, then load the corrected accounts back.
Run the spend-integrity reconciliation (reconcile_monthly_totals) much more often than its current cadence.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the on-call paging rotation for io-shop.
Make the io-shop deploy pipeline require the test suite to pass before any revision is deployed.
Add a review checklist rule: a change that stops writing a stored field must list every reader of that field and show each one no longer depends on it.

causal_chain.step: No failure was seen by anyone using the shop, and takings held. What was seen instead: the spend-integrity check found that shoppers' stored month totals did not match the purchases behind them.

Purchases written after the onset were stored without moving the account's month total. At the revision that ran, record_purchase and record_purchase_deriving_the_month both append the purchase and add only to total_cents, so total_this_month_cents stayed where it was whichever path the purchase took.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy P1 of revision 4c810f22: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after P2 at {P2.1}, so the service did no harm while P1's revision was running.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the window read before the onset.

causal_chain.step: That write path arrived with deploy P2 of revision 26f1d7e2 at {P2.1}, which removed the month-total update from record_purchase. All {T10.2} replicas were running that revision as of {T10.1}.
The change stopped writing total_this_month_cents but kept the field, and the statement, summary and reconciliation code still read the stored value as the month's spend.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change stopped the shop from updating each shopper's saved spending-this-month figure when they bought something, while the parts of the shop that show and check that figure still read the saved copy.

contributing_factors.factor: Month-total drift was watched only by the spend-integrity check, which runs every {A5} days. The module itself says nothing in the write path notices when a total and the purchases disagree.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A reconciliation run much more often, or a check at write time, would have caught the drift soon after the deploy, before most of the affected purchases were written.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An on-call person would have been asked straight away to take the rollback Argus left for a person, rather than it waiting.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: By Code-Fix's reading, the test file at the deployed revision holds a test that pins record_purchase adding to the month total, which the deployed code no longer does. No test run before the deploy was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A required test run would likely have failed on the change and stopped it before it reached production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: No review was seen that checked who still reads total_this_month_cents before the change stopped writing it, even though the module's own docstring warns that a write moving one copy and not the other leaves two answers.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A reviewer listing the field's readers would have seen that the statement, summary and reconciliation still read the stored value, and stopped the change.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the rollout state and found every replica running the revision deployed just before the onset.
The Investigator Agent read that deployment's diff, which showed the month-total update taken out of record_purchase.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone else before the onset, ruling out a flag flip.
Argus declined to roll back when nothing could tell it whether the rollback worked, and left the rollback for a person instead.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request, with tests and a one-off repair script.

input.root_cause: Revision 26f1d7e2 took the update of total_this_month_cents out of record_purchase, on the idea that the month's spend would be worked out from the purchase history. But the Account still carries the stored field, and the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation still read that stored value instead of working it out. Since record_purchase_deriving_the_month never moved the field either, every current-month purchase written after the deploy left the stored month total short by its price, whichever path wrote it.
input.still_at_risk: The month totals already saved short stayed wrong, and each new purchase this month could leave them further short, so monthly statements and spend summaries could keep showing shoppers less than they spent; a shopper routed through the month-deriving write path could see the same drift even after a rollback.
input.symptom: Shoppers saw no failure, but their stored monthly spend totals stopped matching their purchases
